title: AlphaGenome 2: Deciphering how cells read DNA to better understand disease
gist: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional DNA-sequence model trained on 107M+ single-cell profiles that predicts variant effects per cell type/state, nearly doubling causal-variant recall on TenK10K (30% vs 16%) and generalizing to unseen cell states without retraining. It ships via API (commercial access in private preview), with precomputed GWAS variant scores, planned Antigravity Skills, and early industry uptake by Genomics Limited's Mystra platform.

insights.claim: Google DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA sequences and variants affect gene expression in hundreds of specific human cell types rather than broad tissue averages.
insights.speaker: Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga Avsec
insights.so_what: Moves AI genomics from tissue-level to cell-level resolution, the granularity where disease mechanisms actually operate.

insights.claim: AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional model that takes a target biological condition (tissue, cell type or state) as input at every architectural stage alongside a million-letter DNA sequence, predicting one condition at a time.
insights.speaker: Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga Avsec
insights.so_what: Conditioning lets one model learn how the same DNA is read differently across cell types and generalize to new conditions.

themes.theme: Benchmark gains on causal variant discovery

insights.claim: On the TenK10K single-cell dataset of 28 primary immune cell types, AlphaGenome 2 identified causal variants at 30% vs. 16% and directional gene effects at 43% vs. 23% compared with fine-tuned AlphaGenome 1 and other specialized tools.
insights.speaker: Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga Avsec
insights.so_what: Near-doubling of variant recall is a step-change that widens the pool of candidate drug targets from existing genetic data.
insights.quote: nearly twice as many causal variants (30% vs. 16%) and directional gene effects (43% vs. 23%)

insights.claim: AlphaGenome 2 computationally reproduced a landmark finding that a distant regulatory variant drives IBD by overactivating ETS2 in gut macrophages, singling out the causal variant while leaving other cell types and genes largely unaffected.
insights.speaker: Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga Avsec
insights.so_what: In-silico replication of known biology is the validation pharma needs before trusting the model on novel targets.
insights.quote: It singled out the causal variant and showed that it selectively boosts the ETS2 gene in gut macrophages

insights.claim: On genome regions outside its training data, AlphaGenome 2 better tracks continuous gene expression changes across cell types, such as blood stem cells maturing into red blood cells and immune lineages.

themes.theme: Zero-shot generalization to new cell states

insights.claim: AlphaGenome 2 generalizes to unseen single-cell experiments without retraining: a scRNA-seq snapshot from just a few dozen cells is compressed into a cell-state representation, and it matches or beats models trained or fine-tuned on those datasets.
insights.speaker: Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga Avsec
insights.so_what: Lowers the cost of applying the model to proprietary datasets, making it more attractive to pharma with private single-cell data.

insights.claim: Given unseen single-cell data from a COVID-19 mRNA vaccine study, AlphaGenome 2 separated vaccine-activated T cells from resting ones and showed a severe-COVID-19 variant disrupts gene activity more strongly in the activated state, an effect missed in unactivated cells.
insights.speaker: Adam Gayoso, Natasha Latysheva, Pushmeet Kohli and Žiga Avsec
insights.so_what: State-dependent variant effects imply many disease variants are invisible in static atlases, a source of untapped target discovery.
